# Worker memory guard — M3 contracts and runner integration in progress

M1 and M2 are complete. **M3 remains in progress.** This record covers the first serial sink-contract seam at `eaeaca55c67efa0da0ea4bcb9168c65254adae26` and its reviewed repair at `049a6df8a13b6925044758ec7bf1461e562e0f14`. Runner activation, durable feedback/outbox reconciliation, owner-only capture/park, lifecycle wiring and their integration proofs are not implemented by this seam. Production enablement remains disabled; calibration and CI timing remain unverified.

## Implemented and executed

- Monitor feedback/preservation callbacks receive the original captured context, abort signal and remaining budget. Runtime enrollment requires a synchronous preparation hook and an explicit independent preservation budget. Pure monitor fixtures retain their compatibility fallback; production runtime does not use that fallback.
- Preparation receives the exact frozen structured intervention result before tool outcome delivery or awaited feedback. This supplies metadata for the future owner's retention/outbox intent even if shutdown prevents later callback dispatch. Local `memoryPark` only retires command authority; it is not API park acceptance.
- Runtime receipts retain unsettled callback promises with their original context and kind. Shutdown joins bounded monitor orchestration, not abort-ignoring callbacks. Receipt retention is in-memory ownership evidence, not durable replay or permission to release clone/session custody. The runner must consume/reconcile it in the next unit.
- Historical callbacks remain bound to their original context, including flight, lifecycle revision, nonce, generation and episode; they do not find a successor by run ID.

After exact-result assertions were strengthened, typechecking and all 76 focused tests passed again (`gate-log.i9k4fg`). Single-file/focused Node checks used `--test-timeout=120000`; gate recipes/settings/concurrency were unchanged.

The repair captures preservation eligibility before preparation and still invokes only the original captured owner afterward. Canonical typecheck/lint/dead-code checks and 77 focused tests then passed (`gate-log.QHApaA`, EXIT=0, zero skips/cancellations).

## Trusted executor bridge, runner integration still pending

At `a35e3e28f0eafae456ba7247daa9b4999497eb42`, trusted `RunContext.capturedMemory` supplies the capability after executor construction. Each Codex provider epoch reads it once before epoch launch and binds that exact snapshot to its default command spawner, root broker and child delegation. An explicitly supplied accessor returning undefined refuses startup instead of falling back to static authority; a different run identity also refuses before credential release. Direct callers without the accessor retain the existing static-option seam. The accessor and capability are excluded from the explicit provider request projection; the test checks that the private nonce is absent from provider requests and emitted messages. This is not exhaustive disclosure-path or production lifecycle proof.

Lead canonical typecheck/lint/dead-code checks passed with four new epoch-seam tests and 18 existing adapter tests, zero failures/cancellations/skips (`gate-log.dEHTKW`, EXIT=0). Reviewer/tester/auditor reviewed the immutable range with no blocking findings. Tester verified typed isolated folds of the bridge, default-spawn binding and broker binding fail named epoch/enrollment assertions; two refusal-path mutation timeouts were explicitly excluded from accepted failure evidence. Auditor's first checkout secret scan was contaminated by concurrent test edits; the fixed original export was checked afresh. No scan of a moving checkout is claimed as proof of the committed candidate.

The original review's child-delegation coverage gap was repaired at `4382e521648d920a8890a2d225b55ef1633649d4`. Its named test drives root dispatch through child demultiplexing and the actual shell callback/spawn seam, with accessor capture A and distinct static capture B. It checks the child's thread/dispatch identity, one accessor read, metadata accepting A and rejecting B, and both callback responses. Lead canonical typecheck/lint/dead-code checks plus all five epoch-seam tests passed with zero skips/cancellations (`gate-log.aBlpLY`, EXIT=0). All three validators found no mandatory defects in the committed repair. Reviewer and tester independently typechecked an isolated fold reverting only delegation's binding to the static option and observed RED at `delegated child shell metadata binds accessor capture A` (`false !== true`), then verified the baseline passes. This closes the coverage note; it does not prove runner activation or preservation. Generic tester suggestions for a formatter/coverage gate remain deferred (two suggestions in the `a35e3e28` report); they do not justify changing existing gate recipes.

**M3 remains in progress.** No production runner/main wiring, live-DB park flow or full M3 integration gate was executed by this bridge unit. The full canonical gate remains pending for the integrated implementation. Production enablement remains disabled.

## Runner integration candidate, full milestone proof pending

The next serial candidate wires the single runtime into the runner. It captures immutable registration/claim/episode/flight authority, carries spent allowance across provider epochs and uses independent phase tokens for approval, input and follow-up waits. A taken human revision may reopen that exact phase without synthesizing an early Running write. Pressure holds are separate from phase holds; monitor selection and pre-signal checks reject changed phases. This is a candidate integration, not a declaration that M3 is complete.

Feedback intent is retained before tool completion; acknowledgement requires joining the original transport. Memory teardown uses the existing durable outbox tail writer with the original generation and sequence, under a separate cleanup budget. Durable storage does not stand in for acknowledgement. Original sink, capture and close promises remain owned after deadline; uncertain work retains clone/session custody. Capture attempts share a single owner deadline and are limited to three. An already-exhausted persisted allowance stops the first accessor and uses the same owner-hold operation without inventing a victim, pressure sample or tool result.

Four focused memory files passed 124 tests, zero failures/cancellations/skips (`gate-log.PrtBXX`, EXIT=0). These use synthetic pressure and an actual runner/fake API; they are not a real Codex adapter or live-DB runner end-to-end proof. The earlier three-attempt regression failed when the memory loop inherited the existing five-attempt recovery constant; the memory-specific loop now has the approved three-attempt bound. Bypassing the initial allowance stop produced a named assertion failure, not a timeout (`gate-log.zK0U3u`, mutation test EXIT=1; harness EXIT=0 after restoring the original source).

## Next serial integration

The full canonical integration gate remains pending for the wired M3 unit; M2's earlier passing gate is historical evidence at its own candidate. Required fake-API/live-DB end-to-end proofs, including missing-preservation-integration sensitivity, remain pending.

Source-only starting points confirmed at M2 completion `f8e407c7`: `main.ts` creates the memory singleton after `RunRunner`; the trusted `RunContext` is constructed in `RunRunner.phasePreflightHandoff` after the flight exists. The runner's two executor factory calls are initial execution and retained-claim replacement. Its state-report choke point and approval/input/abort/rearm/teardown paths need captured lifecycle handling. The executor bridge now consumes the trusted accessor, but the runner does not supply it yet. Backend memory park already exists, while runner/state-request typing still needs captured `register_nonce` and `memory_episode`. `MessageBatcher.emit` rejects post-close emission, so delayed feedback cannot assume that ordinary emission is durable. These are bounded source-map starting points, not an exhaustive control-flow audit or completed design/runtime proof.

Use existing bounded capture/ownership and custody paths, retain source/session intent before waits, and mark parked only on authoritative acceptance. Reconcile unfinished owner operations before any clone/session release; late callbacks must not mutate a successor. M4 owner surfaces, M5 isolated calibration/local timing/final gates and lander-owned post-publication CI timing acceptance remain pending.
